key_insight: Data-free PINNs capture weak deep-cavity recirculation with floor-region velocity discrepancies below 5%, but accuracy varies by region and observable.
engineering_relevance: Regional validation is essential when assessing cavity-flow predictions because bulk velocity agreement can obscure errors in weak recirculation and rotational fields.
method: Hard-constrained streamfunction PINNs for steady 2D incompressible flow at depth-to-width ratio 5 and Re = 100–1000.
Prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants.
Validation against independent spectral/hp reference solutions with the same Gaussian-regularized lid.
evidence_signal: Across four Reynolds numbers, evaluation on a 121×605 grid found 5.130–7.850% interior velocity discrepancies; a separate 161×801 assessment at Re = 1000 reduced this discrepancy from 5.624% to 2.658% with the refined workflow.
watch_item: Improvements reflect accumulated training changes rather than an isolated sampling effect, and substantial rotational-field discrepancies remain.
paper_title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
